passages.text: What, then, is the advantage of being a Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision?
passages.sermon:
A Jew is a person from the people of Israel.
Circumcision is a physical sign given to the Jews by God.
Someone may ask, “What is the advantage of being a Jew?”
Someone may also ask, “What is the value of circumcision?”
passages.original: Τί οὖν τὸ περισσὸν τοῦ Ἰουδαίου ἢ τίς ἡ ὠφέλεια τῆς περιτομῆς

passages.text: Much in every way. First of all, they have been entrusted with the very words of God.
passages.sermon:
Jews have many advantages in every way.
God gave Jews many blessings.
First, God entrusted Jews with His words.
God gave Jews His very words to keep and share.
passages.original: πολὺ κατὰ πάντα τρόπον πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ ὅτι ἐπιστεύθησαν τὰ λόγια τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: What if some did not have faith? Will their lack of faith nullify God’s faithfulness?
passages.sermon:
Some people did not have faith.
Their lack of faith does not cancel God’s faithfulness.
God remains faithful even if some do not believe.
passages.original: Τί γάρ εἰ ἠπίστησάν τινες μὴ ἡ ἀπιστία αὐτῶν τὴν πίστιν τοῦ Θεοῦ καταργήσει

passages.text: Certainly not! Let God be true and every man a liar. As it is written: “So that You may be proved right when You speak and victorious when You judge.”
passages.sermon:
God is always true.
Everyone may have told a lie before.
If someone has told a lie, then could they be called a liar?
Therefore, every person is a liar.
When God speaks, God will be shown right.
When God judges, God will win.
This is written in Scripture.
passages.original: μὴ γένοιτο γινέσθω δὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἀληθής πᾶς δὲ ἄνθρωπος ψεύστης καθὼς γέγραπται Ὅπως ἂν δικαιωθῇς ἐν τοῖς λόγοις σου καὶ νικήσεις ἐν τῷ κρίνεσθαί σε

passages.text: But if our unrighteousness highlights the righteousness of God, what shall we say? That God is unjust to inflict His wrath on us? I am speaking in human terms.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking.
Paul is addressing Christians in Rome.
Paul asks a question.
The righteousness of God is seen more clearly when compared to our unrighteousness.
What should we say about this?
Should we say that God unjust when He brings His wrath on us?
Those questions are a human way of speaking.
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀδικία ἡμῶν Θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην συνίστησιν τί ἐροῦμεν μὴ ἄδικος ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ἐπιφέρων τὴν ὀργήν κατὰ ἄνθρωπον λέγω

passages.text: Certainly not! In that case, how could God judge the world?
passages.sermon:
If God were unjust, then He could not judge the world.
However, God judges the world.
So God is always just.
God cannot be unjust.
God must be just to judge all people.
passages.original: μὴ γένοιτο ἐπεὶ πῶς κρινεῖ ὁ Θεὸς τὸν κόσμον

passages.text: However, if my falsehood accentuates God’s truthfulness, to the increase of His glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?
passages.sermon:
God is always truthful.
God’s truthfulness brings Him glory.
I am a human being.
I have lied before.
My lie made God’s truthfulness stand out more.
Therefore my lie brought more glory to God.
If my sin increased the glory of God, why does God still judge me as a sinner?
If my sin increased the glory of God, why am I still condemned?
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ ψεύσματι ἐπερίσσευσεν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ τί ἔτι κἀγὼ ὡς ἁμαρτωλὸς κρίνομαι

passages.text: Why not say, as some slanderously claim that we say, “Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is deserved!
passages.sermon:
Some people slander us.
They claim that we say, “Let's do evil to bring about good.”
We do not teach doing evil to bring about good.
God will judge those who slandered us.
Their condemnation is just.
passages.original: καὶ μὴ καθὼς βλασφημούμεθα καὶ καθώς φασίν τινες ἡμᾶς λέγειν ὅτι Ποιήσωμεν τὰ κακὰ ἵνα ἔλθῃ τὰ ἀγαθά ὧν τὸ κρίμα ἔνδικόν ἐστιν

passages.text: What then? Are we any better? Not at all. For we have already made the charge that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin.
passages.sermon:
Paul asks if being a Jew is better than not being a Jew.
No, being a Jew is not better than not being a Jew.
The law of God accuses both Jews and Greeks.
Both Jews and Greeks are under sin.
Therefore all people are under sin.
No group of people is free from sin.
The law of God accuses everyone of having sinned in their life.
passages.original: Τί οὖν προεχόμεθα οὐ πάντως προῃτιασάμεθα γὰρ Ἰουδαίους τε καὶ Ἕλληνας πάντας ὑφ’ ἁμαρτίαν εἶναι

passages.text: As it is written: “There is no one righteous, not even one.
passages.sermon:
No one is righteous.
Not even one person is righteous.
This is written in Scripture.
passages.original: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Οὐκ ἔστιν δίκαιος οὐδὲ εἷς

passages.text: There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.
passages.sermon:
No one understands.
No one seeks God.
passages.original: οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ συνίων οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ ἐκζητῶν τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.”
passages.sermon:
All people have turned away from God.
All people have gone astray from God their Shepherd.
All people have together become worthless.
No one does good.
Not even one person does good.
passages.original: πάντες ἐξέκλιναν ἅμα ἠχρεώθησαν οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ ποιῶν χρηστότητα οὐκ ἔστιν ἕως ἑνός

passages.text: “Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.” “The venom of vipers is on their lips.”
passages.sermon:
The throats of sinners are like open graves.
Sinners use their tongues to deceive.
Venom, like that of vipers, is under the lips of sinners.
passages.original: τάφος ἀνεῳγμένος ὁ λάρυγξ αὐτῶν ταῖς γλώσσαις αὐτῶν ἐδολιοῦσαν ἰὸς ἀσπίδων ὑπὸ τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν

passages.text: “Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness.”
passages.sermon:
Sinners speak with their mouths.
The mouths of sinners are full of cursing.
The mouths of sinners are full of bitterness.
passages.original: ὧν τὸ στόμα ἀρᾶς καὶ πικρίας γέμει

passages.text: “Their feet are swift to shed blood; ruin and misery lie in their wake, and the way of peace they have not known.”
passages.sermon:
Sinners act with violence, such as shedding blood.
The feet of sinners move quickly to shed blood.
Sinners cause harm wherever they go.
Ruin follows sinners.
Misery fills the paths of sinners.
Sinners do not know the way of peace.
passages.original: ὀξεῖς οἱ πόδες αὐτῶν ἐκχέαι αἷμα σύντριμμα καὶ ταλαιπωρία ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν καὶ ὁδὸν εἰρήνης οὐκ ἔγνωσαν

passages.text: “There is no fear of God before their eyes.”
passages.sermon:
Sinners do not fear God.
Sinners do not respect God.
Sinners do not see God as holy.
Sinners do not honor God in their hearts.
Sinners do not keep God in their thoughts.
Sinners do not care about what God wants.
Sinners do not let God guide their actions.
Sinners do not look to God for wisdom.
Sinners do not see God’s authority before them.
passages.original: οὐκ ἔστιν φόβος Θεοῦ ἀπέναντι τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν

passages.text: Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.
passages.sermon:
The law of God speaks to people who are under the law.
The law of God gives commands and instructions to us.
We know this is true.
The law speaks for a purpose.
The law makes every mouth silent.
No one can make excuses before God.
No one can boast before God that they perfectly fulfilled His law.
The law shows that the whole world is accountable to God.
Everyone must answer to God.
passages.original: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι ὅσα ὁ νόμος λέγει τοῖς ἐν τῷ νόμῳ λαλεῖ ἵνα πᾶν στόμα φραγῇ καὶ ὑπόδικος γένηται πᾶς ὁ κόσμος τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: Therefore no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law. For the law merely brings awareness of sin.
passages.sermon:
No one can become righteous before God by doing works of the law.
The law does not make people righteous.
The law shows people what sin is.
The law brings knowledge of sin.
passages.original: διότι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται πᾶσα σὰρξ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ διὰ γὰρ νόμου ἐπίγνωσις ἁμαρτίας

passages.text: But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, as attested by the Law and the Prophets.
passages.sermon:
God has revealed His righteousness.
The righteousness of God is separate from the law.
The Law and the Prophets testify about the righteousness of God.
passages.original: Νυνὶ δὲ χωρὶς νόμου δικαιοσύνη Θεοῦ πεφανέρωται μαρτυρουμένη ὑπὸ τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν προφητῶν

passages.text: And this righteousness from God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe. There is no distinction, for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
God gives righteousness.
God gives righteousness through faith in Jesus Christ.
God gives righteousness to all who believe.
God does not make any distinction between people.
God does not make any distinction those who are Jews and those who are not.
Both Jews and those who are not Jews have sinned.
All people have sinned.
All people fall short of God’s glory.
God justifies people freely by His grace.
God justifies us through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
passages.original: δικαιοσύνη δὲ Θεοῦ διὰ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς πάντας τοὺς πιστεύοντας οὐ γάρ ἐστιν διαστολή πάντες γὰρ ἥμαρτον καὶ ὑστεροῦνται τῆς δόξης τοῦ Θεοῦ δικαιούμενοι δωρεὰν τῇ αὐτοῦ χάριτι διὰ τῆς ἀπολυτρώσεως τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: God presented Him as the atoning sacrifice through faith in His blood, in order to demonstrate His righteousness, because in His forbearance He had passed over the sins committed beforehand.
passages.sermon:
God presented Jesus Christ as the sacrifice to atone for our sins.
God did this so people could receive forgiveness through faith in the blood of Jesus.
God wanted to show His righteousness.
God had been patient.
God had passed over sins committed before.
God did this to make His righteousness clear.
passages.original: ὃν προέθετο ὁ Θεὸς ἱλαστήριον διὰ τῆς πίστεως ἐν τῷ αὐτοῦ αἵματι εἰς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ διὰ τὴν πάρεσιν τῶν προγεγονότων ἁμαρτημάτων ἐν τῇ ἀνοχῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: He did this to demonstrate His righteousness at the present time, so as to be just and to justify the one who has faith in Jesus.
passages.sermon:
God acted to show His righteousness now.
God is just.
God justifies everyone who has faith in Jesus.
God is just and Justifier.
passages.original: πρὸς τὴν ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν δίκαιον καὶ δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἐκ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith.
passages.sermon:
Boasting has no place.
God excludes all boasting.
God does not exclude boasting by a principle of works.
God excludes boasting by faith.
If our works saved us, then we could boast.
Because we're saved by faith, then we cannot boast.
Because we're saved by faith, we give glory to God and not to ourselves.
passages.original: Ποῦ οὖν ἡ καύχησις ἐξεκλείσθη διὰ ποίου νόμου τῶν ἔργων οὐχί ἀλλὰ διὰ νόμου πίστεως

passages.text: For we maintain that a man is justified by faith apart from works of the law.
passages.sermon:
God justifies people.
We are justified by faith.
We are not justified by works of the law.
We believe this is true.
We become right with God through faith apart from works of the law.
Works of the law do not make us right with God.
passages.original: λογιζόμεθα γὰρ δικαιοῦσθαι πίστει ἄνθρωπον χωρὶς ἔργων νόμου

passages.text: Is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles too? Yes, of Gentiles too, since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.
passages.sermon:
God is not only the God of the Jews.
God is also the God of the Gentiles.
There is only one God.
The same God Who is over the Jews is also over the Gentiles.
God will justify the circumcised by faith.
God will also justify the uncircumcised through the same faith.
passages.original: Ἢ Ἰουδαίων ὁ Θεὸς μόνον οὐχὶ καὶ ἐθνῶν ναὶ καὶ ἐθνῶν εἴπερ εἷς ὁ Θεός ὃς δικαιώσει περιτομὴν ἐκ πίστεως καὶ ἀκροβυστίαν διὰ τῆς πίστεως

passages.text: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians about faith and the law.
Paul asks a question.
Does faith nullify the law of God?
No, faith does not nullify the law of God!
Instead, we uphold the law of God.
passages.original: Νόμον οὖν καταργοῦμεν διὰ τῆς πίστεως μὴ γένοιτο ἀλλὰ νόμον ἱστάνομεν
